engine.powerNote: 81 PS (59.6 kW) @ 10,250 rpm, 64 Nm @ 6,250 rpm; 2025 update added Sport mode, cornering ABS/TC, Triumph Shift Assist and cruise control as standard

chassis.brakes: Twin 310 mm front discs with 2-piston sliding calipers, 255 mm rear disc, optimised cornering ABS
chassis.suspension: Showa 41 mm USD separate-function big-piston (SFF-BP) forks; Showa monoshock with preload adjustment

price.note: Based on the German list price (UVP) of EUR 8,295 for the 2025 model; UK price GBP 7,895 OTR. Romanian importer pricing not published online.

a2Note: 59.6 kW natively, but Triumph offers an official A2 restrictor kit in European markets that can be fitted and removed by a dealer.
beginnerNote: One of the friendliest middleweight nakeds: light, low-ish seat and a forgiving throttle, though 81 PS still deserves respect as a first bike straight after the licence.
whoFor: New or returning riders who want one bike that commutes all week and entertains on Sunday, with real triple-cylinder character and a full modern electronics suite at a fair price.
notFor: Maybe not for you if you need wind protection and luggage capacity for regular two-up touring.
about: The Trident 660 is Triumph's entry-point roadster, built around a 660cc triple that combines low-down twin-like torque with a free-revving top end. The 2025 update added cornering ABS and traction control, a quickshifter, Sport riding mode, cruise control and My Triumph connectivity as standard. It remains light-steering, compact and confidence-inspiring, with premium Showa suspension unusual at this price.
pros: Charismatic, flexible 81 PS triple engine
2025 spec adds quickshifter, cornering ABS/TC and cruise control at no extra cost
Neutral, easy handling with quality Showa suspension
Official A2 restrictor kit available
Strong value against Japanese rivals
cons: Modest wind protection and practicality typical of a naked
805 mm seat may be tall for shorter riders
sources: Triumph Motorcycles official press release and technical specification for the 2025 Trident 660 (triumph-mediakits.com)

engine.powerNote: 65 PS (47.8 kW) @ 7,500 rpm; high-torque 270-degree Bonneville twin with 80 Nm at just 3,800 rpm

chassis.brakes: Single 320 mm front floating disc with 4-piston radial caliper, 255 mm rear disc, optimised cornering ABS
chassis.suspension: 43 mm Marzocchi USD forks; twin Marzocchi piggyback rear shocks with preload adjustment

price.note: Based on the German list price (UVP) of EUR 9,995 for the 2025 model (multicolour schemes +EUR 350); UK price GBP 9,195 OTR.

a2Note: 47.8 kW natively; an official accessory restrictor kit brings it within the 35 kW A2 limit.
beginnerNote: Low 780 mm seat, soft low-rev torque and unintimidating manners make it one of the easiest 'big' bikes to start on; only its 216 kg wet weight asks for some care at walking pace.
whoFor: Riders who value timeless Bonneville style with modern reliability, an easy-going torquey twin, and a low seat - ideal as a stylish first big bike or a relaxed weekend machine.
notFor: Maybe not for you if you want sharp modern-naked performance or plan long motorway trips - the 12-litre tank and upright ergonomics limit range and comfort at speed.
about: The Speed Twin 900 is Triumph's most accessible Modern Classic, thoroughly updated for 2025 with USD Marzocchi forks, an aluminium swingarm, piggyback rear shocks and cornering ABS. The 900cc high-torque parallel twin majors on relaxed low-rev grunt rather than outright power. It blends genuine retro looks with a slim new bench seat and a discreet TFT-hybrid dash.
pros: Effortless 80 Nm of torque from low revs
Low 780 mm seat suits shorter riders
2025 chassis upgrade: USD forks, aluminium swingarm, piggyback shocks
Timeless styling with modern electronics and A2 kit option
Frugal 4.0 l/100km published consumption
cons: 216 kg wet is porky for the class
sources: Triumph Motorcycles official press release and technical specification for the 2025 Speed Twin 900 (triumph-mediakits.com)

engine.powerNote: 130 PS (95.6 kW) @ 12,000 rpm with Moto2-derived engine internals; 80 Nm @ 9,500 rpm

chassis.brakes: Twin 310 mm floating front discs with Brembo Stylema 4-piston monobloc calipers, 220 mm rear disc, cornering ABS
chassis.suspension: Fully adjustable Showa 41 mm big-piston USD forks; fully adjustable Ohlins STX40 piggyback monoshock

price.note: Based on the German 2025 list price of EUR 12,795 for the Street Triple 765 RS.

a2Note: 95.6 kW output is far beyond A2 limits and no restricted version is offered.
beginnerNote: A 130 PS track-bred hyper-naked with razor throttle response and a tall 836 mm seat - superbly rewarding for experienced riders, but too fast and too sharp to learn on.
whoFor: Experienced riders who want near-supersport pace and track-day ability in an everyday naked package, with top-shelf Ohlins/Brembo hardware and Moto2 pedigree.
notFor: Maybe not for you if you are new to bigger bikes, ride mostly two-up, or want a relaxed commuter.
about: The Street Triple 765 RS is the sharpest series-production Street Triple, its 765cc triple developed alongside Triumph's Moto2 race engines and delivering a category-leading 130 PS. The chassis pairs fully adjustable Showa big-piston forks with an Ohlins STX40 shock and Brembo Stylema calipers. At 188 kg wet with aggressive geometry, it is a genuine track-capable naked that remains civil enough for the road.
pros: 130 PS Moto2-derived triple with ferocious top end
Ohlins/Showa/Brembo Stylema chassis hardware as standard
Light 188 kg wet weight and agile geometry
Full IMU electronics with track mode and quickshifter
cons: Tall 836 mm seat and committed riding position
Premium price for a middleweight naked
Firm suspension setup for everyday roads
sources: Triumph Motorcycles official press release and technical specification for the 2023-on Street Triple 765 RS (triumph-mediakits.com)

engine.powerNote: 34.9 kW (47 bhp) @ 7,250 rpm and 52.3 Nm @ 5,150 rpm from the air-cooled 270-degree SOHC twin

chassis.brakes: 320 mm front disc, 240 mm rear disc, dual-channel ABS
chassis.suspension: 41 mm telescopic forks; twin gas-charged rear shocks with adjustable preload

price.note: Based on Romanian importer list prices of roughly EUR 7,000-7,500 depending on colour/wheel variant; UK prices GBP 6,599-7,099.

a2Note: 34.9 kW output is natively within the 35 kW A2 limit - no restrictor needed; Royal Enfield markets it as A2-ready.
beginnerNote: Docile throttle, flat torque curve and neutral handling make it a superb A2-friendly first big twin; its 217 kg kerb weight and modest ground clearance are the only real caveats.
whoFor: Riders who want authentic 1960s roadster style and a characterful, unstressed twin at a bargain price - especially A2 licence holders who never want to feel short-changed.
notFor: Maybe not for you if you expect modern electronics, strong outright performance or light low-speed handling.
about: The Interceptor 650 (INT 650 in some markets) is Royal Enfield's retro roadster twin, built around an air-cooled 648cc parallel twin with a 270-degree crank and a slick 6-speed gearbox. It delivers its 47 bhp gently and tunefully, backed by a steel double-cradle frame tuned with input from Harris Performance. Simple, honest and affordable, it has been one of Europe's best-selling A2 machines since 2019, gaining LED headlamp and alloy-wheel options in its latest update.
pros: Characterful 270-degree air-cooled twin with easy torque
Natively A2 compliant - no restriction kit needed
Outstanding value and simple, robust engineering
Classic styling with quality chrome tank options
Neutral, stable handling
cons: Heavy for its class at 217 kg kerb
Basic suspension and brakes by modern standards
No rider aids beyond dual-channel ABS
Limited wind protection for motorway work
sources: Royal Enfield UK official Interceptor 650 technical specification PDF (royalenfield.com)

engine.powerNote: 14.87 kW (20.2 bhp) @ 6,100 rpm and 27 Nm @ 4,000 rpm from the air-oil-cooled J-series single

price.note: Romanian distributor (ASP Group East) lists the Meteor 350 from EUR 4,500; UK prices GBP 4,099-4,249 by variant.

a2Note: 14.87 kW is far below the 35 kW A2 limit; also rideable on an A1-upgraded progression path in some markets thanks to its modest power-to-weight.
beginnerNote: About as unintimidating as real motorcycles get: 765 mm seat, gentle 20 bhp, smooth fuelling and relaxed cruiser ergonomics - a nearly foolproof first bike.
whoFor: New riders and easy-going commuters who want laid-back small-cruiser style, a very low seat and sub-3 l/100km running costs, with the Tripper navigation pod as a practical bonus.
notFor: Maybe not for you if your riding regularly includes motorways - the official top speed is 114 km/h, so overtaking reserve is minimal.
about: The Meteor 350 is Royal Enfield's budget-friendly small cruiser, powered by the smooth J-series 349cc air-oil-cooled single with an unusually refined long-stroke character. It carries genuine cruiser proportions - 19-inch front wheel, teardrop tank, low 765 mm seat - plus a digi-analogue dash with the Tripper turn-by-turn navigation pod fitted as standard from MY24. Performance is modest but delivery is friendly, and fuel economy of 2.79 l/100km gives a huge range from the 15-litre tank.
pros: Very low price point and running costs
Low 765 mm seat and light controls ideal for beginners
Refined, vibration-free 350 single for the class
Tripper navigation and dual-channel ABS standard
500 km+ realistic range from 15-litre tank
cons: 20 bhp means limited motorway and overtaking ability
5-speed gearbox and official 114 km/h top speed
191 kg is not light for 20 bhp
sources: Royal Enfield UK official Meteor 350 technical specification PDF (royalenfield.com)
